items.stem: Why constrain model output to a defined schema in an extraction pipeline?

options.text: Downstream code can rely on a predictable, parseable shape
options.rationale: Correct: a schema makes output structure predictable for downstream consumers.

options.text: It guarantees the extracted values are factually correct
options.rationale: A schema constrains shape, not factual correctness of values.

options.text: It removes the need to validate the output
options.rationale: Validation is still needed; models can still deviate or omit fields.

options.text: It makes the model cheaper per token
options.rationale: Schemas do not change token pricing.

items.explanation: Correct: a schema makes output structure predictable for downstream consumers.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A structured response is missing a required field. What is the safe action?

options.text: Reject or recover from it; do not pass it downstream
options.rationale: Correct: failing validation must stop bad data from propagating.

options.text: Insert it into the database as-is
options.rationale: Storing invalid data corrupts downstream systems.

options.text: Assume the field is empty and continue silently
options.rationale: Silently assuming values hides data-quality failures.

options.text: Disable validation to avoid the error

items.explanation: Correct: failing validation must stop bad data from propagating.

items.stem: Which TWO practices protect consumers when an output schema must change? (Select TWO)

options.text: Version the schema so old consumers keep working
options.rationale: Correct: versioning avoids breaking existing consumers on a change.

options.text: Validate output against the correct schema version
options.rationale: Correct: validating per version keeps the contract enforceable.

options.text: Change the contract silently in place
options.rationale: Silent changes break downstream consumers without warning.

options.text: Stop validating to speed things up
options.rationale: Dropping validation lets malformed data through.

items.explanation: Correct: versioning avoids breaking existing consumers on a change.
